title: Ferry transportation before the bridge or when the bridge was closed
description: A ferry, located a mile south of Hartland, connected the east side of the river to Victoria Corner on the west, once an important stagecoach stop well before Hartland had its name. When the eastern spans and pier of the bridge were lost in 1920, ferry service resumed at this historic crossing, a mile below Hartland, where the steady current made it ideal for a cable ferry. The approaches on both banks could easily be made passable for teams and automobiles. Construction of a new ferry boat began in Hartland in May 1920, with the cable soon to arrive. The ferry operated daily from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. The image here shows the rustic ferry crossing the St. John River to Upper Victoria Corner. Arthur Hovey operated the ferry; the woman in the photo remains unidentified.
